paras.text: … was done. The members also presented their proposals and recommended such a system in which human rights are respected. Measures of help and redress for the victims of racial discrimination were also proposed.

paras.text: For the effective resolution of conflicts the practical strategy of arbitration or mediation can also be adopted. In this respect the United Nations holds great importance. The Arab–Israel issue has given birth to several sub-conflicts. Because of differences over the use of the water of the River Jordan between Israel and Syria, and of the area vacated by the army, border clashes took place between the two countries. In the same way differences of Syria, Egypt, Lebanon and Jordan with Israel further increased. To control these affairs the United Nations made attempts at mediation but could not be successful. In the year 1967 a six-day war took place between the Arabs and Israel, in which the Egyptian air force was destroyed on the very first day of the war. Israel occupied the Gaza Strip and the Sinai peninsula. Israel also occupied East Bait-ul-Muqaddas, the West Bank of the River Jordan and the Golan areas. In November 1967 the Security Council of the United Nations, through resolution number 242, asked Israel for a conditional withdrawal from the occupied areas. The condition was that the Arab countries also recognise Israel and live in peace with it. However the parties were not ready to accept these conditions.

paras.text: In 1947-48 the United Nations issued orders of ceasefire to stop the war going on in Kashmir between India and Pakistan. The United Nations established between Azad and Occupied Kashmir a temporary line by the name of the Line of Control (LOC). For the supervision of this line a United Nations supervisory military group was brought into being, and along with it this too was recognised: that the Kashmiris have the right of self-determination to decide their political future. But the parties, especially India, remain stuck on their stubbornness, and instead of the issue being solved it is becoming more complicated. The United Nations is an important institution for resolving world problems and conflicts, but the need is that this institution be made empowered so that it can get its decisions accepted.

Mediation

For the effective resolution of conflicts the practical strategy of arbitration or mediation can also be adopted. In this respect the United Nations holds great importance. The Arab–Israel issue has given birth to several sub-conflicts. Because of differences over the use of the water of the River Jordan between Israel and Syria, and of the area vacated by the army, border clashes took place between the two countries. In the same way differences of Syria, Egypt, Lebanon and Jordan with Israel further increased. To control these affairs the United Nations made attempts at mediation but could not be successful. In the year 1967 a six-day war took place between the Arabs and Israel, in which the Egyptian air force was destroyed on the very first day of the war. Israel occupied the Gaza Strip and the Sinai peninsula. Israel also occupied East Bait-ul-Muqaddas, the West Bank of the River Jordan and the Golan areas. In November 1967 the Security Council of the United Nations, through resolution number 242, asked Israel for a conditional withdrawal from the occupied areas. The condition was that the Arab countries also recognise Israel and live in peace with it. However the parties were not ready to accept these conditions.

In 1947-48 the United Nations issued orders of ceasefire to stop the war going on in Kashmir between India and Pakistan. The United Nations established between Azad and Occupied Kashmir a temporary line by the name of the Line of Control (LOC). For the supervision of this line a United Nations supervisory military group was brought into being, and along with it this too was recognised: that the Kashmiris have the right of self-determination to decide their political future. But the parties, especially India, remain stuck on their stubbornness, and instead of the issue being solved it is becoming more complicated. The United Nations is an important institution for resolving world problems and conflicts, but the need is that this institution be made empowered so that it can get its decisions accepted.

If world leaders come forward with truthfulness and honesty, then any problem can be ended.

Functions of International Court of Justice

The International Court of Justice, or World Court of Justice, is a key part of the United Nations. This court was established in 1945 in the light of the charter of the United Nations. This court works in the light of the charter of the United Nations. It resolves legal problems among member countries, and it also gives legal opinion to the United Nations and its various agencies on questions relating to international law. Its headquarters is in the city of The Hague in the Netherlands. All the member countries of the United Nations can approach this court. A non-member too can become a party to it in that situation when that country accepts the conditions laid down by the United Nations and contributes to the court’s expenses.

A case can be brought into the court in two ways. The first way is that the parties, with mutual consent, present their issue to the court. The second way is that one party presents an application unilaterally to the court, when the applicant is confident that the opposing party, in the light of some agreement, is bound to accept the court’s decision. The parties announce beforehand that they will accept the court’s decision. While deciding, the court takes the support of international law. The court’s decision has to be accepted by the parties, and the right to appeal against it is not available to any party. If any party does not act upon the court’s decision, then in the light of the United Nations charter the Security Council has the authority to take measures to enforce the decision.
